text:
Jonathan Marchessault came back from injury on November 17 and has two goals and three points in three games since, including a goal and an assist against Pittsburgh. The season line, 8 points in 17 games, leans heavily on the power play: five of those points came with the extra man. In a Tennessean headline he "reveals secret to Nashville Predators' third-line success," and third line is the right description of his role now, at about 16.5 minutes a night.

Five on five is where the concern lives. The Predators have had 39.7% of the expected goals, our measure of chance quality, with him on the ice, 10.25 points worse than without him, and his teammates have scored about 3.7 more goals than those chances suggest. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season, with opponents getting more chances against him than almost any forward (bottom 3%). Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking agrees that his value isn't in creating offense at even strength. He's 35 and a former Conn Smythe winner; our numbers project 38 points.
headline: Marchessault is producing on the power play
